rv.q: Oleanna is a fast-moving, exquisitely infuriating experience over 80 minutes.
In Bailey's confident hands, Oleanna is something of a Trojan horse.
The great thing about Lucy Bailey's 80-minute production, designed by Alex Eales, is that it changed my mind about the power balance in the drama.

It's an exciting performance of a riveting story that is worth seeing, but I again find myself contrasting the play's peculiar version of the world with the reality of how difficult it is for people to get anywhere complaining to institutions.
Slinger tempers the role with a leavening softness that accentuates the plight of someone placed on a fast track toward destruction.

cn.t: Lucy Bailey's revival of Mamet's provocative campus drama remains powerfully unsettling, with critics praising its even-handed direction and edge-of-seat tension, though some question whether it ultimately sides against women's complaints.
